title: Introduce streaming deglitch filter and OpenAI-compat shim for microburst payloads
author: Maya Liu
description:
Motivation: We observe intermittent consumer-facing glitches when the gateway proxies many tiny fragments (short bursts of 1-10 byte payloads) from OpenAI-compat clients calling tool/fncall streams. These microbursts cause: increased connection churn, spurious fncall boundary signals, and occasional buffer-triggered drops when proxies attempt strict framing. This PR introduces a lightweight in-proxy "deglitch filter" and a small compatibility shim to smooth microburst arrival patterns without changing the external API semantics.

What this changes: single continuous description below —
- Add deglitch filter: coalesces closely spaced fragments (configurable time window and cumulative size threshold) before passing them into the stream writer. The filter is conservative: it never holds fragments longer than window_ms (default 12ms) and never exceeds size cap (default 8KB) before flushing. The goal is to reduce pathological writer wakeups while preserving low-latency for normal traffic.
- Introduce microburst-compatible framing fallback: when downstream indicates strict OpenAI-compat framing is required (older clients), the shim emits explicit fragment boundary markers while still applying the deglitch coalescing to avoid excessive tiny writes.
- Add route-level tunables in gateway route config: deglitch.window_ms and deglitch.max_coalesce_bytes with sane defaults and per-route overrides for high-throughput toolcall routes.
- Wire new metrics and tracing: gateway.deglitch.flushed_count, gateway.deglitch.coalesce_ns_p50/p95, gateway.deglitch.drop_events (should be zero), and trace events for coalesce decisions.
- Tests and harness: unit tests for timing edgecases, integration test that replays real traffic traces with microbursts, and e2e against the OpenAI-compat CLI to validate fncall handshake stability.

Why this approach: previous attempts increased write buffer sizes (caused tail latency regression under normal load) or added complex per-connection heuristics that diverged between hosted and private installations. Deglitch filtering provides predictable smoothing with explicit route-level controls and observability so operators can tune behavior for different client populations.

Backwards compatibility: Default behavior preserves current semantics for most routes. The shim is enabled for OpenAI-compat routes by default but can be disabled per-route. No changes to the public OpenAI-compatible API surface are required.

Testing and outcomes: In the canary cluster with production traces, we measured a 42% reduction in stream aborts tied to fragment churn, a 9% drop in writer wakeups per second, and negligible change to median stream latency (+1ms). Tail latency (p95/p99) is unchanged within measurement noise.

Migration notes and ops guidance: Operators can start on safe defaults. For paths serving many tiny tool calls (e.g., agent debug tools), bump deglitch.max_coalesce_bytes to 16KB and consider lowering window_ms to 8ms if the workload is ultra-low latency. Release notes appended below.

Related: ENG-4221 for the broader streaming stability epic, SUP-719 incident thread that motivated the microburst replay harness.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for coalesce logic and time window behavior
- [x] Integration tests replaying recorded microbursts
- [x] Metrics + dashboard tile proposal in observability-pack (linked in ticket)
- [x] Docs update in redwood-docs describing route-level tunables (separate PR incoming)
commits_summary:
4 commits:
- add deglitch filter implementation and unit tests
- expose per-route config and default values
- add metrics, tracing events, and integration test harness with recorded microburst traces
- compatibility shim for strict-framing clients and small refactors to stream writer tests
review_thread: Arjun Patel (2026-02-19): Can we make the default window_ms configurable at runtime without a restart? Some private customers will want to tweak quickly.
Maya Liu (2026-02-19): Good call. I exposed window_ms and max_coalesce_bytes via the per-route config which can be hot-reloaded by the route-manager. Documented in config comments.

Sofia Martinez (2026-02-20): The coalesce logic looks fine but I'm worried about ordering guarantees when we emit shim boundary markers. Have you validated that fncall boundaries cannot be observed out of order?

Maya Liu (2026-02-20): We preserve fragment ordering; the shim only inserts explicit markers in-band and flushes in-order. Added unit tests to assert boundary ordering under jitter. See integration test microburst_replay.rs.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-22): CI flaked on the integration test once (timeout). I reran it locally with a longer test timeout and it passed. Recommend bumping the test timeout to avoid flakes in CI.
Maya Liu (2026-02-22): Increased the harness timeout and added a jitter seed to make the test deterministic across runs. CI rerun succeeded.
release_notes: Gateway: Add deglitch filter to smooth microburst fragment patterns for OpenAI-compat streaming routes. Improves stream stability under high-fragment churn while preserving API semantics. Route-level tunables: deglitch.window_ms, deglitch.max_coalesce_bytes.
